title: Inversion Thinking
subtitle: ou want to stress-test a plan before committing to it. Forward thinking hasn't revealed the
useWhen: problems. You need a completely different angle of attack.
howToUse: Inversion means solving a problem backwards. Instead of 'how do I succeed?' you ask 'what would guarantee I fail?' Then systematically avoid everything on that list. Charlie Munger called it one of the most useful thinking tools he knew. It surfaces risks that positive thinking consistently misses. Listing paths to failure is concrete and finite, while listing paths to success is easy to fool yourself with. The founders who last usually wrote the failure list first and took it seriously.
steps: Define what you're trying to achieve be specific.
Ask AI to list everything that would guarantee you fail at that goal.
Review honestly. Cross off what you've already mitigated.

For everything remaining, build one prevention action each. What would guarantee failure? Now avoid that. Charlie Munger built Berkshire Hathaway's risk culture around inversion. Before every major investment, the team asked: 'What would guarantee we lose money here?' That list of failure conditions became the due diligence checklist. Not pessimism precision. Most investors ask 'why will this work?' Munger asked 'what would make this fail?' first. IN PRACTICE
promptBody:
Act as a strategic risk advisor using inversion thinking.
Goal        :   [WHAT I AM TRYING TO ACHIEVE  be specific]
Context  :   [SITUATION, INDUSTRY, STAGE, TEAM]
Step 1      :   List everything that would guarantee I fail. Think broadly - execution,  
                     market, team,  timing, assumptions, behaviour.
Step 2     :   Rank these failure causes by probability.
Step 3     :   For the top 5, give one specific prevention action I can take 
                    before moving forward.

proTip:
Share the failure list with your team before launch. Ask each person to add one item you
missed. The combined list will contain at least one thing that would have actually stopped
you  and now it won't.
